title: Coflex: Enhancing HW-NAS with Sparse Gaussian Processes for Efficient and Scalable DNN Accelerator Design
problem: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search (HW-NAS) suffers from extensive search spaces and high computational costs, limiting practical adoption for DNN accelerator design.
motivation: Efficient HW-NAS enables automated co-optimization of neural networks and hardware for edge accelerator development.
method: Coflex combines a Sparse Gaussian Process (a model that learns from past accelerator designs to predict which new designs will work well) with multi-objective Bayesian optimization (a search algorithm that balances competing design goals). It simplifies the mathematical calculations from cubic to near-linear complexity, making the model much faster while keeping predictions accurate. This enables efficient exploration of large design spaces that would otherwise require prohibitive computational cost.
key_novelty: Sparse Gaussian Process combined with multi-objective Bayesian optimization reduces accelerator design search complexity from cubic to near-linear, making large-scale exploration practical.
contributions: SGP-based HW-NAS framework with near-linear kernel complexity
Multi-objective Bayesian optimization for hardware-aware architecture search
1.9x to 9.5x computational speed-up over state-of-the-art methods
High network accuracy with improved Energy-Delay-Product
limitations: SGP approximation may not capture all design space nuances for highly constrained accelerator scenarios.
